question: True or false: a square contains exactly as many points as one of its sides?
answer: True. Cantor proved it in 1877, in letters to Dedekind. Pair each point of the square with one number by interleaving the digits of its two coordinates; with care over decimals like 0.1999…, which equals 0.2, the pairing works exactly. A solid cube, or all of space, holds no more points than a line segment.
move: Bigger in size and more in number are different questions.
trap: Thinking a square must hold more, since it holds whole lines of points.
reference: Gouvêa, Was Cantor Surprised?, American Mathematical Monthly, 2011
